themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 12 this week versus a baseline average of 5.4 per week—a 123% increase—suggesting a sudden environmental and public health problem emerging in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park over the past 7 days.
evidence: 12 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.96)
123% spike above baseline indicates sudden deterioration, not gradual trend
Aligns with broader sanitation concerns: 1,224 unsanitary condition complaints and 10 residential disposal complaints (344% spike last week)
reporting_angles: Map dumping hotspots and speak with residents in affected areas about repeat offenders or known dumping sites
Contact DSNY to determine if enforcement or collection schedules have changed; compare street sweeping data week-to-week

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Safety Issues
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 5 this week from a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 344% spike—raising questions about restaurant/food vendor health and safety compliance in the district this week.
evidence: 5 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.18)
344% spike suggests acute food safety or hygiene failures rather than chronic issues
Convergence with illegal dumping spike may indicate broader waste/sanitation management breakdown affecting food vendors
reporting_angles: Identify which establishments filed complaints; contact DOHMH for recent inspection records and violations
Interview food vendors about supply chain disruptions, waste collection, or pest control challenges this week

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Two street sign issues spiked simultaneously this week and last week: dangling signs (3 complaints, +700% vs. 0.4 baseline) and missing signs (3 complaints 3 weeks ago, +243% vs. 0.9 baseline), indicating potential systematic infrastructure neglect across the district.
evidence: Dangling street signs: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, +700%)
Missing street signs: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, +243%)
Pattern suggests deferred maintenance or recent weather event damaging signage across multiple blocks
reporting_angles: Walk key commercial and residential corridors to photograph and catalog missing/dangling signs; identify geographic concentration
Request DOT maintenance schedule and ask why sign replacement or repair requests are not being addressed promptly

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints surged to 12 last week from a baseline of 3.5 per week—a 243% increase—indicating a potential pest control crisis in Kingsbridge/Bedford Park over the past 1-2 weeks.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints last week vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.91, +243%)
Converges with illegal dumping spike (123% this week) and residential disposal complaints (+344% last week), suggesting conditions attractive to rodents
Sustained elevated complaints signal ongoing infestation rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Interview residents about where rodents are sighted most frequently; ask about building conditions and waste management
Contact DOHMH and HPD to cross-reference rat baiting schedules and building violation history; assess if response is adequate

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints exploded to 3 from a near-zero baseline of 0.1 per week three weeks ago—a 2300% spike—creating potential safety hazards across the district.
evidence: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, +2300%)
Highest z-score of all spikes, indicating extremely anomalous event
Likely seasonal (late summer/early fall growth) but severity of spike warrants investigation into whether Parks Dept. maintenance is keeping pace
reporting_angles: Locate the 3 specific blocks with overgrown trees; photograph hazards and assess if they obstruct streets, sidewalks, or utilities
Request Parks Dept. tree trimming work orders and backlog for CD 207; determine if budget or staffing constraints are delaying maintenance
